title: Per-item refusal events let a sender set the log's size
description:
Several WARN and INFO events fire once per item on a path whose volume
a sender controls, so a hostile or broken peer sets the log's size.

| event | level | per | site |
|---|---|---|---|
| `agent_message_discarded` | warn | received message | mimid-agent-store/src/sync.rs:1036 |
| `live_stream_frame_refused` | warn | stream frame | mimid-agent-core/src/stream.rs:301 |
| `fanout_delivery_refused` | warn | delivery | mimid-server/src/hub/fanout.rs:265 |
| `catch_up_refused` | warn | catch-up answer | mimid-server/src/follower/notify.rs:390 |
| `agent_jmap_push_too_large` | warn | push | mimid-agent-jmap/src/push_deliver.rs:225 |
| `group_info_too_large` | info | request | mimid-server/src/hub/group_info.rs:133 |
| `welcome_too_large` | info | Commit | mimid-server/src/hub/update.rs:945 |

A sender that submits ten thousand messages with a past `expires`
writes ten thousand WARN lines, at the level an operator watches.

## Not simply a level to lower

Each of these is worth knowing. A discarded message is one the user
will never see, and `agent_message_discarded` already pushes the same
fact into `report.problems`, so the front end tells the user
regardless. The question is which channel carries the per-item detail
and which carries the fact that it is happening at all.

## What the answer probably is

mimid has a metrics facility now (`telemetry::metrics`, bead
mimid-ndov), which did not exist when these events were written. A
counter per refusal reason answers "how often" without a line each,
and a periodic summary answers "is this happening now" for an operator
reading the log. Keep the per-item event at DEBUG for the operator who
is looking at one sender.

Per event, decide: a counter, a periodic summary, a DEBUG event, or
some pair of those. Do not lower a level without putting the fact
somewhere an operator still sees it.

## Why this is a decision and not a cleanup

Lowering a WARN an operator may already alert on is a visible change,
and `welcome_too_large` is named in docs/operating.md as an example of
what to alert on. Whatever is decided goes in that document too.

The metrics-label rule in telemetry.rs's Limitations binds the answer:
a counter must not be labelled by anything an unauthenticated sender
chooses, so "refusal reason" has to come from a fixed set.
